comment: Probably 30 parking spaces at this location, but there are 3 other parking lots along the route where it meets the road if you’re willing to start at a different point. The only bathroom is where I started the hike. Part of the whirlpool trail is closed, which was difficult but still passable today. I can see how this would get dangerous easily if conditions were wet.

Beautiful views! I went to this trail back on Victoria day long weekend. It was VERY busy. Make sure to come early for a parking spot. The trail is very easy to follow, but be aware of people who boulder as they were blocking pathways. But otherwise, very fun to watch them! Great rest areas on rocks near the water for lunch. Worth the drive from GTA for sure!!
Niagara Glen portion is fun and easy, the Whirlpool section is mostly rock scrambling and a never ending workout. Great balance! Great trails. Would deff not recommend dogs.
Extremely nice!!!

Best to avoid the Karen’s that look like they work here and make you avoid all the extra fun little trails like the trail to the whirlpool. They said that we weren’t allowed to go down there but we did anyways Gray trail. Just enjoy it.

Whirlpool trail is closed at the moment! We tried to use the trail anyway but after 1.5 km it was completely blocked by trees and there was no clear route anymore. I recommend just doing the part at the lower part of the river
Trail is sometimes hard to find and slick, but the views are amazing.
If you decide to do the whole loop just take care in the whirlpool trail, it’s pretty rocky

The most strenuous hike I’ve ever done. I ran out of water and my phone died for the last mile ish. I have a battery pack but forgot the cord. I loved the views. Seriously nothing more beautiful but you should have proper hiking boots, maybe poles if you are older like myself with bad knees and lots of water on a hot day. I loved the challenge but almost couldn’t complete it. It was super hard. Lots of rock scrambles and obstacles to navigate through, around and over. Not for the faint of heart or anyone out of shape to attempt as a first hike. Bring snacks and be prepared.
Great hike, easy but also some technical aspects to keep it interesting. Nice views and lots of varying tree types!
incredible! 5/5!

Whirlpool trail is close.  
Thus great trail, views. Some heat but also cool spots along the boulders.
So awesome!
The whirlpool section is “closed” so be careful!
If you’re from southern Ontario you have no excuse to not see this
Spectacular scenery, but extremely technical

Always great and the most dynamic and technical trail in the area. Currently not a lot of bugs and not a lot of mud pits, but wear long pants for the occasional ivy on the trail.  There are some new downed trees over the winter near the whirlpool that I hope they'll clear.
Easy access to trail from multiple parking (paid) lots. Clear trail markers, but lower section requires some rock scrambling. Great views along the river, especially from the top sections.
This trail was lovely but technical.  Intermediate might not be accurate.

This part is currently closed and should be avoided after or during a rainy day. There are many very slippery parts but it's totally doable during nice weather. The last stairs part is funny and is the only challenging part of the trail. 
You can do it but be careful on your steps.
Pretty muddy in some parts, one mile section between the whirlpool and the main glen trail was a little tougher than the rest of the loop

Really cool features and views. Take some time at the whorl pool. Not shown but whole loop was completed and I'd say that any fit person can do this trail in the winter with the proper boot. Nothing extra needed. Parking is nice and Easy but does not take cash. Nature centre is not open in the winter but hey. On the way out of the loop snow is quite deep and not compacted meaning we walked the top section on the road. 8/10 thanks for reading.
Beautiful trail. Lots of up and down and challenging no areas. Slippery with the slushy snow but well worth it.
Conditions are snowy or mucky for most of the trail, but the ice has started forming around the waterfall rock section. Cramp ons are pretty much a must right now.
Not in good condition with lots of leaves, ice and snow melt. Whirlpool section is hard with some scrambling
Amazing views!
Beautiful trail for a fall day! Certain parts definitely get your heart pumping!
Got there early so you can find a parking space. The hourly rate is 8 dollars. Or just pay annual pass for 30 dollars. 2025 water is too low due to lack of raining.

Nice with the fall colours, and not busy at all.

Hard to stay on path at some points along with the leaves making it more difficult than normal.

Great trail!
Pretty long
Great conditions right now. We're not quite peak colour but with all the rain coming this week this might be the best we get this year. Wear hiking boots for the best trail in the area.
Beautiful!! If you’re doing the whole loop — some of the trail is not very well maintained in the middle. Push through though! The trail IS there lol
Fun hike!  Lots of rocks and roots, so not ideal for some older and younger hikers, or those who are not sure-footed.
Bring drinking water and few energy bars
Beautiful views, mostly shaded and a pleasant breeze throughout. Tricky in certain areas but not too bad. Great hike!!

The upper part of the loop was completely unremarkable and part of the bottom loop is closed (the whirlpool trail itself). I would recommend spending more time on the glen main loop as well, it was very pretty.
Very slippery around and adrenaline filled whirlpool but fantastic
Love river views and rocky trail!
This trail at times was quite difficult. Great views though!

Great trail overall. There are various other trails that connect to the main loop which also offer great views. We especially loved the whirlpool trail section. Some sections can be a little tricky if you don’t have proper footwear. There is some litter along the way which was disappointing, but overall would highly recommend this trail.
Amazing hike today
Moderate difficulty

Deep descend into the gorge so remember what goes down has to come up . Lots of water, backpack and hiking shoes are highly recommended. I didn’t find it that difficult in general but it would definitely be hard for a new hiker in some areas. We did 2 and a half hours of the trail was beautiful and had a nice workout lol.

August 2nd, 2025 completed. 
Beautiful views of the river. Recommend walking to the water to view to rapids and whirlpools up close and wait for the whirlpool boats to come by. 
Would NOT do this trail during or after rain fall. Technical in some sections. Get ready to walk up and down man made stairs and rock stairs. Some reviews mentioned it’s dog friendly, I would suggest otherwise- it can be done if really needed to but wouldn’t be friendly on their paws.
Great summer hike!! Would not try in we conditions.

This is one of the best trails I’ve done in Ontario so far. It’s my second time and it was as much fun as the first time. The boulders are so interesting, the river is rapid and beautiful, there are fun scrambles , expect to get wet as there are little waterfalls along the way, and the parking is very expensive, but it’s worth it so much fun

I completed the Niagara Whirlpool (Long) Loop with my friends Carly & Austin to celebrate my 23rd birthday. The hike had many pretty lookouts along the Niagara whirlpool and rapids. On the route, there were many boulders that were labeled, some for beginners and others for more experienced climbers. The long loop specifically is VERY rocky. In my opinion, not all dogs would be able to complete the trail. I also recommend not to go during rainy days as the rocks are REALLY slippery when wet. Towards the end of the trail, there are SO MANY stairs. Me and my friend had to take breaks to catch our breath on the way up. If you are not up for the challenge, I recommend following the route in the opposite direction so that you can decline down the stairs instead. 
Note: Parking is expensive! The rate is $8/hr and we paid $16 for the 2 hour hike.
Rocky in some spots, some good spots to swim. Tough climb towards the end but good all in all.

Beautiful views.
Lots of parking, but paid hourly.
Whirlpool rapids trail not clearly marked, so be careful. 
Great and short hike!

Parked in Lot C Upper Rapids Road by far the cheapest parking in the area. Plus we wanted to walk with the river and rapids to get to HorseShoe Falls (about 1 mile). Walked to the Rainbow Bridge and back. States at 9 am and finished after 12 pm with the pups. By noon, was getting very crowded.

Trail closed for section near whirlpool.  Can get to either side but not across.

Otherwise good.  Lots of stairs.  Some rocky sections that would be slippery if wet but no problem today.
Km 3-4.5 was almost no trail, very difficult there. Everything else was very nice.
Amazing trail, however it’s not the time mentioned. We did half of it and took us 1 hour and 50 minutes (and we are not slow pace hiker)

We did this hike counter clockwise, which I highly recommend. Once you get down the big staircase to the water, the trail markings are not obvious. About three quarters of the way around the whirlpool, there are suddenly a bunch of rock scrambles with wet and slippery rocks. At this point the trail is marked with faint yellow blazes/lines. The scrambles could be difficult for an inexperienced hiker. Good boots with traction are recommended! The scrambles continue off and on for much of the rest of the trail near the water. 

The trail is very narrow in places and if I didn’t have the map downloaded we would have been lost several times. Trail markings aren’t great. 

It’s a beautiful hike with spectacular views. The river and gorge are stunning. I can’t recommend it enough but folks should know what they are getting themselves into!

Around the Whirlpool, the trail markings weren’t so great and the trail wasn’t so visible. Also, it was very close to the edge and very slippery. Overall, this trail I really enjoyed the great scenery. You do have to pay for parking.
Beautiful hike
Beautiful trail with amazing views of river. Lots of poison ivy. Rocky in many places - good hiking boots or shoes a good idea.
Incredible views and the opportunity to swim in the river. But the hike turned out to be very difficult for me…
10% of the trail  was muddy, rest was dry. Not busy on a Friday morning.  One of my favorite hikes in Ontario.

Lovely hike… had to rush it to avoid getting a ticket because I only paid for 2hrs. I will suggest parking for longer period if you love take pictures. Trail was lovely and I would definitely do it again.

Beautiful trail with lots of good spots to take pictures. Expect all sort of terrain, rocky, little muddy, elevation and also we crossed sort of small waterfalls.   Overall it was really nice.  Not too hard.
Amazing trail I love it

Gorgeous trail. The views along the river portion of the trail are amazing, there is really nothing like it in the area. I've lived in southern ontario my entire life, can't believe it took me this long to discover this trail. The trail is dog friendly but the whirlpool section definitely has some trickier areas that would be tough for any pups with mobility issues or lacking confidence.

We did the main trail loop and the whirlpool trail. The trail is Extremely rugged. Good hiking boots recommended. There are stairs on both the sides of the trail. However the stairs on the whirlpool trail is much harder. Be prepared to walk on all different terrains. There were muddy parts, streams and even going in front of a waterfall. So rain jacket is recommended. Overall it was an amazing hike the trails are very beautiful. It took us 3.5hrs to complete the trails. But we stopped quite a few times for photos.

The pantaloon flowers are out, and the whirlpool trail is clear to walk through. It's a little tricky at spots, trying to climb over rocks etc. but a lot of fun and you get right up next to the water. A surprising amount of dead fish that have washed up and make it smell in certain areas but on a better note, a lot of natural clay, all different colours all along the path!
Conditions are very good right now, with very few mud pits outside the area near the valley by the wooden stairs up the escarpment. Still the most fun trail in the Niagara region.
Good winter conditions, but be prepared with good grip winter hiking boots and icers. We had the whole trail for ourselves. I will never get tired of this amazing trail.
Such an awesome hike if you love jumping from rock to rock and exploring
Make sure to wear hiking shoes, trail is uneven and rocky paths. Wear comfortable fit.

Great trial. Note that a couple of spots have wet rocks by the coast line. Be careful for the inexperienced. 

Definitely recommend this trail.

This is one of my favourite trails. Great views. Trail conditions are good. It is a moderate trail and definitely requires appropriate footwear. Dog friendly besides that I had to carry my dog down the metal spiral stairs.
Trail condition good. Easy trail
Very rocky on the whirlpool section so be careful. Beautiful trail

Keep coming back to this, it is a lot challenging to hike the whirlpool trail, there may parts that need to climb, loose rocks and steep hills, one slip you are in the niagara lake. I call it dangerous, not for kids, do not take your girlfriend to show off, Make sure you are fit and well prepared if you take my route. I go there almost once a month, love it

Beautiful afternoon, chill breeze with sun. Liked the hike… I went counterclockwise; if you’re going to do the full loop, I recommend doing the same that way you’re with the road at the beginning and have serenity from there on out finishing the hike along the river and up through the rocky forest. Pack a snack!! A LOT of sublime spots to setup for a picnic, read a book or just listen, observe and relax.

Nice loop. A little busy near the start and end but not a lot of traffic if you do the full Nice loop. A couple of tricky, rocky spots but definitely moderate. To those that say it’s more I recommend sticking to walks in your neighborhood.

This trail is always a blast, in every season. I did the "extended" version once again to get to the fun uphill rock section ("purple trail"). Conditions are currently extremely icy throughout, so bring your cramp-ons. If you need extra balance, bring poles too. The rocky waterfall section is totally do-able without going around, but it's very technical and you must be very careful. Without cramp-ons or chains it's near impossible. All inclines and declines are covered in ice. This makes the trail extra challenging and lots of fun, but do it carefully. Plan on 2-3h on your parking meter just due to the carefulness/technicality required to complete.

One of my favourite hikes.
